functions.function_source:
func TestCreateDestroyErrors(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct{ name, in, want string }{
		{"create never bound to a message", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
create participant C
participant D", "must be followed by a message"},
		{"create at end of diagram", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
create participant C", "must be followed by a message"},
		{"created participant uninvolved", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
create participant C
A->>B: y", "must receive the message"},
		{"created participant sends its own creating message", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
create participant C
C->>A: hello", "must receive the message"},
		{"create reuses an existing id", "sequenceDiagram
A->>C: x
create participant C
A->>C: y", "id already exists"},
		{"create reuses a declared id", "sequenceDiagram
participant C
A->>B: x
create participant C
A->>C: y", "id already exists"},
		{"destroy uninvolved", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
destroy A
B->>C: y", "not involved in the following message"},
		{"destroy unknown participant", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
destroy Zed
A->>B: y", "unknown participant"},
		{"destroy at end of diagram", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
destroy A", "must be followed by a message"},
		{"create requires participant or actor", "sequenceDiagram
A->>B: x
create C
A->>C: y", "invalid syntax"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := Parse(c.in)
			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
				t.Errorf("want error containing %q, got %v", c.want, err)
			}
		})
	}
}
